subject: MaplePay: missing text in some completions - follow-up & closure
messages:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@maplepay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@maplepay.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (no subject) — intermittent missing tail text in completions

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a few production requests from our users where the assistant output seems to abruptly truncate mid-sentence — not a hard error, but the response ends without the closing paragraph. It happens maybe 1-2% of calls for a specific flow (refund verification). I attached a sample payload and a short snippet from our client console.

Example: prompt id 20270525-07d9f — the generation stops after "Please confirm the refund date is" and there's no follow-up. We retried client-side and sometimes the call returns full text; other times it's short.

Can you please confirm whether this looks like an issue on your side or something on our SDK/network? We have request IDs and timestamps if you need them.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Tan
Head of Integrations, MaplePay
alex.tan@maplepay.com
Attachment: example_request_payload.json (json, 2.1 KB)
Attachment: client_console_log.txt (txt, 8.5 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@maplepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: intermittent missing tail text in completions

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and for the payload + logs. That's exactly the kind of repro info we need.

Quick ask while we triage: can you also share any request IDs from your server logs that match the timestamps (UTC preferred) and indicate whether the calls that returned short output used streaming or non-streaming mode? If you can, please paste up to three full request ids and the exact response bodies you observed.

I've looped in Marissa (infra) and Sean (support) to look through service logs and routing. We'll treat this as high priority but note that intermittent, partial completions can be caused by multiple factors (client timeout, connection drop, early close on the socket, or upstream model truncation).

We should have an initial read within 48 hours. In the meantime: please keep the original artifacts (request ids, timestamps, any proxy logs).

—Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Alex Tan <alex.tan@maplepay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: intermittent missing tail text in completions — initial triage

Hi all — quick update from infra after searching the storage and request logs for the time ranges/IDs provided. We investigated the three request ids Alex supplied (20270525-07d9f, 20270525-08a2c, 20270525-10f11):

- No matching server-side request entries found for those IDs in our ingestion logs or S3 persistence. Our access logs show activity from MaplePay IPs during the window, but the unique request IDs in the sample payloads don't appear in our trace index.
- No correlated error spikes, queue drops, or worker restarts in the region during the reported times.
- For the flows you described, the runtime would either stream tokens or return a single completion. We checked model-side logs and there is no sign of truncated generation for matching sessions.

Given the lack of server-side evidence, our leading hypotheses are: 1) the client generated a synthetic local request id that doesn't match Redwood's request-id header, and the short output is from an interrupted client socket; or 2) a proxy between MaplePay and our edge stripped/altered the response before the client wrote it to disk.

Next steps we recommend for reproducibility:
- If possible, capture the Redwood request-id header returned in the response (X-Redwood-Request-Id) and share it; that is the canonical id we use to find entries in our logs.
- Test the same call with streaming disabled (or enabled) to see if behavior changes.
- Run a short cURL from an ephemeral host (outside your proxy) to rule out intermediary manipulation; example curl provided below.

Example cURL (non-streaming):
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @example_request_payload.json 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions

If you prefer, we can run a short joint session with your engineering team to reproduce live. We can also set up request sampling on the edge for your account for 48 hours if you want us to capture full headers and bodies for any future requests.

No platform evidence of truncated model outputs at this time. Please attach any X-Redwood-Request-Id values if you get them.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa Cole
SRE — Inference Platform, Redwood Inference
Attachment: triage_notes-20270528.txt (txt, 1.2 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@maplepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: intermittent missing tail text in completions — final update

Hi Alex / Jordan — following Marissa's look through logs and the lack of any matching Redwood request ids or service-side truncation, we don't have evidence of a platform-side generation truncation. To summarize:

- We searched for the request ids and timestamps you provided and found no server-side match.
- No correlated infra events or model-truncation traces in the timeframe.
- Our best current explanation is client-side or intermediary interruption (timeouts, socket close, proxy buffering).

Recommended immediate actions for MaplePay:
1) When it happens again, capture the X-Redwood-Request-Id from the response headers and forward it to us. That header is our key to locate the exact server-side transaction.
2) Try the call outside of any proxy (direct cURL) to see if the payload returns whole.
3) Temporarily switch streaming on/off for the flow and verify differences.

As a gesture for the uncertainty here, I'm offering to enable request sampling on your account for 72 hours (no charge) so we can capture a wider set of headers/bodies from the edge and correlate quickly. If you'd like that, reply and we'll schedule it for this week.

If you gather a Redwood request id or a server-side log line, we'll reopen an investigation immediately. Otherwise, we'll consider this incident closed on our side but remain available if further evidence appears.

Appreciate the detailed report and sorry for the friction — we want to make sure your integration is rock-solid.

—Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
